name: serial-console-mcp
display_name: Serial Console (telecom, radio, any serial port)
description: Let Claude configure telecommunication equipment and any other device over its serial console.
long_description: An MCP server for serial ports. Drives Juniper Junos and Cisco IOS / IOS-XE console and craft ports, Icom CI-V and Kenwood, Yaesu and Elecraft CAT transceivers, GS-232 antenna rotators, and anything else on a serial cable, in raw, ANSI or VT100 mode. A background reader drains the port the whole time it is open, so reads end at the device's prompt instead of a guessed delay. Includes device presets, control lines (DTR/RTS/BREAK), expect sequences, session capture, baud detection, and operating skills for Junos and IOS.

tools.name: list_serial_ports
tools.description: List every serial port the computer can currently see.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: Show the device presets `connect(preset=...)` understands, with their settings.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Open a serial port and start its background reader.

tools.name: reconnect_last
tools.description: Reconnect to a remembered port with the same settings as last time.

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Close a serial port and free it for other programs.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Report every open port: settings, reader state, buffered bytes, control-line states, capture, and which connection is current.

tools.name: send_text
tools.description: Send an ASCII command to the device.

tools.name: send_hex
tools.description: Send raw bytes given as hex.

tools.name: read_until_prompt
tools.description: Read accumulated output until a prompt appears, or until timeout.

tools.name: read_available
tools.description: Drain and return whatever the device has sent, without transmitting anything.

tools.name: query_text
tools.description: Convenience: clear the buffer, send an ASCII command, and read the reply.

tools.name: expect
tools.description: Run a scripted sequence of send-and-wait steps in one call, like `expect`.

tools.name: clear_buffer
tools.description: Discard any buffered received data.

tools.name: send_keys
tools.description: Press keys by name, encoded the way a VT100/xterm terminal sends them.

tools.name: screen
tools.description: Show the current terminal screen of a vt100/xterm connection: what a person at a real terminal would see right now, as rows of text, plus the cursor position.

tools.name: set_lines
tools.description: Set the DTR and/or RTS output lines and hold them.

tools.name: pulse_line
tools.description: Drive DTR or RTS to `level` for `ms` milliseconds, then restore it.

tools.name: send_break
tools.description: Send a BREAK condition (TX held low) for `ms` milliseconds.

tools.name: capture_start
tools.description: Start writing this connection's traffic to a file until capture_stop.

tools.name: capture_stop
tools.description: Stop the capture started by capture_start and report the file and size.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Return the tail of everything received on a connection since it was opened.

tools.name: port_in_use_by
tools.description: Report which program currently holds a serial port (macOS/Linux, via lsof).

tools.name: detect_baud
tools.description: Try common baud rates on a closed port and rank them by how readable the reply is.

tools.name: civ_build
tools.description: Build an Icom CI-V frame as hex, ready for send_hex.

tools.name: civ_parse
tools.description: Decode Icom CI-V frames from hex (as returned by read_available).

tools.name: civ_freq
tools.description: Convert between a frequency in MHz and CI-V BCD data bytes.

tools.name: cat_build
tools.description: Build a ';'-terminated text CAT command (Kenwood, Elecraft, Yaesu) for query_text or send_text with line_ending="NONE".

tools.name: cat_parse
tools.description: Decode ';'-terminated text CAT replies: rig id to model, FA/FB to MHz, MD to mode name, IF to frequency/mode/VFO/split/TX state, and the ?; E; O; error answers.

tools.name: rotator_build
tools.description: Build a Yaesu GS-232A/B rotator command for send_text (CR) or query_text.

tools.name: rotator_parse
tools.description: Decode a GS-232 reply into azimuth/elevation degrees ("+0180", "+0180+0045", "AZ=180 EL=045") or the ?> rejection.

read_only.title: Read-only mode
read_only.description: Refuse anything but read-style commands (show/display/get, two-letter CAT reads, CI-V read frames) and refuse DTR/RTS changes.

idle_minutes.title: Close an idle port after (minutes)
idle_minutes.description: Free a port nobody has used for this long, so a forgotten connection stops blocking other programs. 0 disables it.
